questions.question_text: Factors for Jute mill concentration along Hugli river.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Proximity to raw jute fields, abundant cheap water for fiber retting, low-cost river transport, cheap labor from WB/Bihar/Odisha, port & banking infrastructure of Kolkata.

questions.question_text: Shift of Sugar industry from North to Western/Southern states.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Sugarcane grown in Maharashtra has higher sucrose content. 2. Cooler coastal climate extends the crushing season. 3. Cooperative sugar mills are highly organized and successful in Maharashtra. 4. Modern machinery in new southern mills yields higher sugar recovery rates.

questions.case_passage:
Industries cause air, water, land, and noise pollution. Effluents discharged into rivers deplete oxygen and poison aquatic life.
Q1. Four types of industrial pollution? (1m)
Q2. Effluent impact on aquatic life? (2m)
Q3. Solution for liquid waste? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Air, Water, Thermal, and Noise pollution.
2. Chemical effluents deplete biological oxygen demand (BOD) and introduce toxic heavy metals that kill aquatic life.
3. Effluent treatment plants (ETP) before river discharge.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Manufacturing Industries: Mineral-Based Industries & Steel Sector

questions.question_text: Second major metallurgical industry in India?
Iron and Steel industry cluster region?
Why is Steel industry called a Heavy Industry?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Both raw materials (iron ore, coking coal, limestone) and finished steel products are bulky and heavy, incurring high freight costs.

questions.question_text: State the raw material proportion for Steel production.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Iron ore : Coking coal : Limestone = 4 : 2 : 1, plus manganese for hardening.
Aluminum is lightweight, resistant to corrosion, good conductor of heat/electricity, malleable, and becomes strong when alloyed with other metals.

questions.question_text: Chhota Nagpur plateau steel cluster reasons & challenges.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Cluster reasons: Proximity to low-cost iron ore, high grade coking coal, limestone, and cheap regional labor.
Challenges: High cost & limited supply of coking coal, low labor productivity, irregular power supply, poor infrastructure.

questions.question_text: Three sequential stages of Industrial Effluent Treatment.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Primary Treatment: Mechanical screening, grinding, flocculation, and sedimentation to remove solid particles.
2. Secondary Treatment: Biological treatment using aerators and activated sludge to digest organic matter.
3. Tertiary Treatment: Chemical treatment, biological recycling, and filtration to achieve zero liquid discharge.

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Textile Value Chain
questions.case_passage:
Textile industry is self-reliant and complete in value chain from raw fiber to finished garments.
Q1. Meaning of 'complete in value chain'? (1m)
Q2. Economic role of textiles? (2m)
Q3. Why spinning is decentralized but weaving is fragmented? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Every stage of manufacturing from raw fiber to garment design takes place within the domestic economy.
2. Contributes significantly to industrial production, employment generation, and foreign exchange earnings.
3. Spinning is concentrated in modern mills, whereas weaving uses diverse traditional handloom/powerloom units.

questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Fitting smoke stacks with electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers. 2. Replacing coal with oil or natural gas fuel.

questions.question_text: Classification of industries on the basis of ownership.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Public Sector: State owned (BHEL, SAIL). 2. Private Sector: Owned by individuals/companies (TISCO, Bajaj Auto). 3. question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Manufacturing Industries: Comprehensive Industrial Economics

questions.marking_scheme_answer: Public: Owned and operated by government agencies (SAIL). Private: Owned and operated by private individuals or corporate entities (TISCO).
Liberalization and foreign direct investment introduced modern global models, boosting demand for passenger cars, 2-wheelers, and commercial vehicles.

questions.question_text: Compare Small Scale and Large Scale industries.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Small Scale: Investment limit up to Rs 1 Crore, uses local labor & smaller machinery. Large Scale: Investment > Rs 1 Crore, employs thousands of workers, complex technology.

questions.question_text: Detailed breakdown of Agro-Based vs Mineral-Based industries with examples.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Agro-Based: Utilize agricultural raw materials. Examples: Cotton, Jute, Silk, Textile, Sugar, Edible Oil. Employment intensive, seasonal link.
Mineral-Based: Utilize mineral ores as raw inputs. Examples: Iron & Steel, Heavy Machinery, Cement, Aluminum Smelting, Chemical & Fertilizers. Capital intensive, heavy freight costs.

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Noise Pollution Control
questions.case_passage:
Machinery noise causes hearing impairment, elevated blood pressure, and stress in industrial plants.
Q1. Health impacts of noise pollution? (1m)
Q2. Mechanical remedies to reduce noise? (2m)
Q3. Personal protective equipment for workers? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Hearing damage, high blood pressure, psychological stress, and heart rate elevation.
2. Fitting silencers on machinery, redesigning equipment, and lubricating moving parts.
3. Earplugs and noise-absorbing earphones.
